sources: codex/CODEX.md v1.0 (120 DK showdown winners 2018-25; 2,761 games 2016-25)

contest_types.label: Single entry / 3-max, under 5k

contest_types.label: 25k+
contest_types.note: dupes are the rake; product of ownership predicts dupes

A.name: Favorite blowout
A.captain: Fav WR1 / fav RB / fav QB - never dog
A.flex: fav QB + fav WR1 + fav RB + fav DST/K; bring-back = dog's single best pass-catcher, never the dog QB

B.name: Favorite controls, competitive (by 4-13)
B.captain: Fav RB (31%) or fav WR1; TE CPT live (21%)
B.flex: RB-CPT template: own WR1 + own TE + own K/DST, opp RB/TE bring-back; low both-QB

C.name: Coin flip / back-and-forth (within 3)
C.captain: Either WR1, either QB; RB less
C.flex: both QBs 43%; both WR1s; K 49% (FG games)

D.name: Dog upset
D.captain: Dog WR1 (the only dog captain that survives), dog RB, dog QB only if he runs
D.flex: dog QB in flex (76%), dog WR1, dog K (52%); bring back fav TE (57% w/ dog-WR CPT) or fav QB (73% w/ dog-RB CPT)

E.name: Shootout overlay
E.overlay: raise both-QB to 50%, TE CPT to ~25%, drop K to ~30% and DST to ~25%

F.name: Grind overlay
F.overlay: DST to 55%, K to 50%, both-QB to 20%, RB CPT to 30%

captain_templates._note: expected flex composition by captain type (winner rates). Used to score 'story fit' 0..1 = fraction of include-items present minus avoid-items present.

QB_FAV._v1.4: Reverted to v1.0 (history re-check, codex/HISTORY_RECHECK_v1.3.md): fav-QB-captain winners had an opp WR 8/15 = 53% vs 71% for other captains; 3-3 only 2/15 (p=0.04). The v1.2 additions came from one 2026 slate.

hard_rules._two_dst_note: v1.3: two DSTs (both defenses, any slot incl. captain) allowed only as a grind-script dart: grind overlay on (total <= 41 or wind >= 10) or total <= 43; never with a kicker; at most portfolio.two_dst_max_per_batch per batch. Evidence (historical winners, not 2026): 5 of 120 winners (4.2%) used both DSTs; 3 of the 5 came from games that finished 17-21 total points; 3 of 19 winners (16%) from games finishing <= 30 had both; 4 of 5 had no kicker. 2026 field corroborates only: field ~2% two-DST, top-1% 14% in NE@SEA (23 total).

soft_penalties._note: penalty points subtracted from the lineup score (score = sim rank percentile or projection z). 1.0 ~ one bucket of the sim ranking.
soft_penalties._opp_wr_v1.4: v1.4: the opp-WR penalty applies to fav QB captains in shootouts again (v1.2 exception reverted). History: in games that scored >=50, fav-QB-captain winners had an opp WR 1/5 vs 26/31 (p=0.009).
soft_penalties._two_k_v1.4: v1.4: two kickers = never (the hard max_kickers 1 already enforced it; the >=52 allowance was dead code and pointed the wrong way: all 3 two-K winners came from lines 41.5-46.5). two_k_min_total kept only for engine compatibility.

share_ceilings._v1.2: k 0.65→0.5: sim wanted K in ~90% of W2 DET@BUF lineups; our batch ended at 76% K; K was in 7% of the top-1%. Codex K rate never exceeds 50% in any total bucket.

ten_laws.law: Leverage lives at captain. Chalk lives in the flex.
ten_laws.evidence: Winners' CPT own median 9.5% (54% under 10%); the same winners carry ~1.5 players >=50% owned and cum own ~204%.

ten_laws.law: Captain the player who can be the game's highest scorer, not the best value.
ten_laws.evidence: Winning CPT median salary $13,500 (1.5x); cheap captains that won scored 2.6x projection.

ten_laws.law: WR and RB win the seat more than the field's QB habit.
ten_laws.evidence: CPT position of winners WR 39 / RB 22 / QB 20 / TE 15 / DST 4 / K 1; field captains QBs 30-35%.

ten_laws.law: Favorite side by default; big favorite = the cleanest rule in the sport.
ten_laws.evidence: Nut CPT from favorite: spread <=3 66%, 3.5-7 58%, >7 80% (RB 44% of those).

ten_laws.law: The dog pocket-QB captain is a graveyard.
ten_laws.evidence: Dog QB at +3.5 or more = nut CPT 3 of 205 games (1.5%).

ten_laws.law: Almost no punts. Winners are not unique because of a $200 guy.
Kickers are in ~half of winning lineups. Never two. Never at captain.
ten_laws.evidence: K in lineup 41% overall, 49% in 2025; double-K 1.1% of top-1%; K captain 1%.

ten_laws.law: Shape follows the spread: 4-2 modal, 5-1 the blowout weapon, 3-3 the field's comfort zone.
Both QBs is a shape, not a leak - in ~1/3 of the batch.
ten_laws.evidence: Both QBs in 34% of winners; 84% in the W2 DET@BUF 72-point shootout, 2-3% in W1 blowouts.
DEN@KC winner shared 1st 102 ways; product of ownership predicts dupes (r^2 0.43).

lessons_2026.lesson: Both-QB lineups and dog captains died; top-1% was 97-100% favorite captain, 5-1 in 89-98%.
Top-1% 84% both-QB, 7% K, 92% no K/DST, 75% two TE. A user lean must never switch off the total overlay (rules v1.2).
Field 47/45/50% on the three stars; every three-star build duplicated 50+ times even in a 20k field. Sim's #1 was a 4% dog-WR captain with both QBs.

engine._note: Inputs for assets/js/showdown_engine.js (the browser port of codex/rules_engine.py) that are not elsewhere in this file. rushing_qbs is parsed from the RUSHING_QBS literal in rules_engine.py; shape_off_template_penalty is the constant in soft_score().

user_leans._note: Ethan's game read as a tilt, applied with --lean. Logged per slate so Tuesday can score the lean vs the no-lean build. v1.2: a lean may shift allocation/shares but may NOT disable a total-based overlay (W2 DET@BUF: 54.5 total, fav_under lean switched the shootout overlay off; game went 41-31, top-1% was 84% both-QB / 7% K).

field_tiers._note: Sunday single-game slates: SUPPORTING evidence only, never pooled with primetime. Same shape as top1pct_by_expected_script.

field_archive._note: Field data = the unified 2026 archive (codex/field_unified.py): complete contest fields from the Stokastic Post-Contest Simulator plus our own DK contest standings, deduped. PRIMETIME slates are the primary cohort; Sunday single-game slates are a separate supporting tier. In the cohort tables the row n IS the number of slates (every lineup in a slate shares one game outcome); rates are the unweighted mean of per-slate rates. Anomalous slates (a QB knocked out early, etc.) are listed but excluded from every table and check. Rules come from the 120 historical winners; this archive only checks them.

rule_verdicts._note: HISTORY FIRST. Every rule on the page comes from the 120 historical DK showdown winners (hist = the winner rate and its n). `check` is the 2026 primetime field archive's annotation — agrees / aligned / split (by script) / mixed / not_enough / watch — never an override: a `watch` item is re-examined in the historical winner data as slates accrue. Effective n = slates. lift / field / top1 arrays align to `slates` (null = not testable or an excluded anomalous slate). Percent points.

check_notes.agrees: the 2026 top 1% sided with this rule against the field in most primetime slates
check_notes.aligned: the 2026 top-1% rate sits in (or near) the rule's batch band
check_notes.split: strong 2026 lifts both ways: the answer depended on the game script
check_notes.not_enough: not enough 2026 primetime slates to check it yet
check_notes.watch: the 2026 sample leans against it: on the watch list, re-checked against historical winners as slates accrue — not a rule change

role_rates._note: Role rates from the HISTORICAL showdown winners (codex/showdown_winners_joined.csv + showdown_slots_joined.csv). cpt.pct = % of winning lineups whose captain holds the role; flex.pct = % with >= 1 player of the role in FLEX; flex.per100 (multi-player roles) = role players per 100 winning lineups; ci90 = 90% Wilson interval in %. "primetime" (TNF/SNF/MNF/Super Bowl) is the default cohort. These are how often a role shows up in winning lineups - not a projection for any game.

depth.note: Winner files hold only the six rostered players, not the slate pool, so depth is reconstructed: salary class from FLEX salary (captain = CPT salary / 1.5), then same-team same-position players in a lineup take strictly increasing depth by salary. Live pools use the true salary rank (engine rank over players not ruled OUT/IR).

calibration_2026.note: share of 2026 DK pool players (FLEX salary >= $1,000) whose salary class equals their true salary rank class; thresholds were fit on the 2026 pools weighted by BB-model ownership

field_gap._note: Field gap per position x side (the 2026 field archive does not split by depth, so every depth role of a family shares its family note). hist = historical primetime winner rate (CPT: captain is that family; FLEX: >= 1 of that family in FLEX). field_2026 / top1_2026 = mean of per-slate rates over the primetime slates (entries pooled across each slate's contests, top 1% cut inside each contest). label: field_gap = field departs >= 5 pts from history AND the top 1% moves >= 3 pts back toward history; field_differs_top1_agrees_with_field = departs, top 1% does not side with history; aligned = within 5 pts. 2026 only annotates; it never changes a rule.

leverage.definition: leverage (pts) = historical role rate - projected ownership of that seat, CPT and FLEX separately
leverage.cpt: cohorts.primetime[.by_spread[bucket]].roles[role].cpt.pct - sum of projected CPT own % of the pool players in that role
leverage.flex: cohorts.primetime[.by_spread[bucket]].roles[role].flex.(per100 if multi else pct) - sum of projected FLEX own % of the pool players in that role
leverage.bucket: use the slate's spread bucket (spread_le3 / spread_3.5_6.5 / spread_ge7 by the favorite's spread) when its n >= min_bucket_n, else the cohort row
leverage.thin_match: flag a player whose FLEX salary is outside depth.salary_by_role[role] p5-p95 (or whose role has < 5 historical salaries): his depth matches the role but his price does not - grey the number, do not headline it
leverage.role_of_player: side = FAV if team == favorite else DOG; depth = salary rank within team+position among players not ruled OUT/IR (QB: 1 -> QB1, 2+ -> QB2+; RB: 1 -> RB1, 2+ -> RB2+; WR: 1, 2, 3+ ; TE: 1 -> TE1, 2+ -> TE2+; K; DST)
leverage.reading: positive = winners used this role more often than the field is projected to; negative = the field is projected to play it more than winners ever did. The historical rate is how often the role is in winning lineups, not a projection. Show the role n and the ci90; when a CI is wider than the leverage, say so.
leverage.ownership_source: public: BirdieBuddy model ownership (pool own / cpt_own). Licensed projections never feed a site number.
